review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its simp interface. Only four declarations carry @[simp]: the `_apply` and `_symm_apply` lemmas for each of the two homeomorphism definitions. All four are `rfl` lemmas. Their left-hand sides are the coerced Homeomorph applied to a point, and their right-hand sides are explicit `⟨p.proj, e p.proj p.2⟩` or `⟨p.proj, (e p.proj).symm p.2⟩`. These orientations are unfolding rules for a named definition, which is the normal choice, and neither right-hand side can be rewritten back to a left-hand side, so I see no credible cycle. The `_apply_proj` and `_symm_apply_proj` lemmas are not simp, and they don't need to be. Once the simp `_apply` lemma fires, the projection of an explicit constructor reduces without any further rule. The two families of lemmas have different head constants. They can both apply only when the complete-field and module-topology hypotheses hold together, and in that case they give the same right-hand side, so they don't compete in a harmful way. The proofs use `simp [A, a, aₗ, h₁, h₂]` and `simp` on goals about local lets. I found no sign that they depend on missing or fragile simp lemmas. I did not run Lean. I also did not check how downstream files use these lemmas, so I can't say whether any simp lemma is missing there.
